subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Automatic Transmissions: Planetary Logic
description: One-minute skill: Automatic Transmissions: Planetary Logic.

hook.text: An automatic transmission shifts without driver input. Clutch packs and brakes rearrange planetary gear paths.

buildup.text: Multiple planetary sets connect in series. Hydraulic clutches lock different elements to create each gear ratio.

discovery.text: A torque converter replaces the clutch pedal. It uses fluid coupling to connect the engine smoothly to the gears.

twist.text: Modern automatics have 8, 9, or even 10 speeds. More ratios keep the engine in its efficiency sweet spot.

climax.text: Today's automatics are often more fuel-efficient than manuals. Computers shift faster and smarter than humans.

punchline.text: Let the computer shift. It's faster than your foot.

quiz.question: How does an automatic transmission change gear ratios?
options: It slides gears along shafts like a manual transmission
Hydraulic clutches lock different elements of planetary gear sets
It changes the size of the torque converter to alter output speed
